The statements can be normalized into directed "ancestor-of" relations (where an edge \(X \to Y\) means "\(X\) is an ancestor of \(Y\)"). The resulting directed graph is a single long chain that includes every individual named in the input.  

One path extracted from the transitive closure begins at Doris and ends at Bobby:  
Doris \(\to\) Abigail \(\to\) Pamela \(\to\) … (via the links Isabella–Donna–Debra–Ethan–…–Joshua) \(\to\) Bobby.  

Consequently Doris lies on the ancestor side of Bobby, i.e., Doris is Bobby’s ancestor.  

No path from Bobby back to Doris exists (Bobby has out-degree 0), so the relation is strictly ancestral rather than one of mutual ancestry, siblinghood, or a common descendant. Options 1, 3 and 4 are therefore false.
